title: Unit – 5 : Session – 9 : SLO – 2  |  Implementation of Shortest Path Algorithm — Code Activities
sections: I. Pseudocode Fill in the Blanks — Dijkstra's
1. Initialize distances of all vertices as INFINITE (INT_MAX), except source = 0.
2. Create a SET (sptSet / visited array) to track visited vertices.
3. For (V-1) times:
a. Pick the vertex u with the MINIMUM distance.
b. Mark u as visited.
c. For all adjacent vertices v: if v not visited and dist[u] + weight(u,v) < dist[v], update dist[v].
II. Complete the C Code Snippet
int minDistance(int dist[], bool sptSet[], int V) {
int min = INT_MAX, min_index;
for (int v = 0; v < V; v++)
if (sptSet[v] == false && dist[v] < min)
min = dist[v], min_index = v;
return min_index;
III. Bug Hunt — 3 Bugs in the Snippet
Bug 1: 'count <= V' runs one extra iteration -> should be count < V - 1 (or < V).
Bug 2: 'sptSet[u] = false' un-marks the picked vertex -> should be sptSet[u] = true.
Bug 3: 'sptSet[v] == true' relaxes only visited vertices -> should be sptSet[v] == false.
Corrected loop:
for (int count = 0; count < V - 1; count++) {
int u = minDistance(dist, sptSet, V);
sptSet[u] = true;
for (int v = 0; v < V; v++)
if (graph[u][v] != 0 && sptSet[v] == false && dist[u] + graph[u][v] < dist[v])
dist[v] = dist[u] + graph[u][v];
IV. Choose the Best Data Structure
Small graph (V <= 10): SIMPLE ARRAY / adjacency matrix — overhead of other structures is not worth it;
O(V^2) is trivially small.
Dense graph (V = 1000, E = 900000): ADJACENCY MATRIX with array-based Dijkstra O(V^2) — E is near V^2,
so heap overhead gains nothing and matrix gives O(1) edge lookup.
Sparse graph (V = 1000, E = 3000): ADJACENCY LIST + PRIORITY QUEUE (min-heap) — O((V+E) log V) is far
better than O(V^2) when E is small; lists store only existing edges.
V. Map the Escape Paths — Paths from vertex 0 to vertex 5
Path 0-1-3-5:            cost 2 + 5 + 15 = 22  <- SHORTEST
Best escape path: 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 5 with total cost 22.
